name: Almanara Electric Trd Co شركة المنارة الكهربائية للتجارة
reason: Almanara (est. 1987, Riyadh HQ, Saudi Arabia) is the sole KSA distributor of Panasonic switches/sockets, Opple and Fumagalli lighting, selling electrical switches & sockets, residential/commercial panel boards, indoor/outdoor lighting and chandeliers. This is electrical wiring/fittings for construction, an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category, regardless of the fact it runs a genuinely live, fully transactional e-commerce site.

name: Almutahidah
reason: Almutahidah (Riyadh HQ, Saudi Arabia, 501-1,000 employees) is a domestic-services company offering hourly home cleaning, trained domestic workers, and licensed drivers. This is a staffing/services business with no product retail of any kind, an outright Gate 2 fail (not a retail category).

name: Aramco Lubricants & Retail Company
reason: Aramco Lubricants & Retail Company is a wholly-owned Saudi Aramco chemicals/lubricants subsidiary (Dhahran HQ) operating under the parent aramco.com corporate site with no dedicated consumer storefront. Petroleum/lubricant and fuel-station retail is not in the approved Gate 2 category list, so it fails category.

name: Cadillac Aljomaih
reason: Cadillac Aljomaih (Aljomaih Automotive Company), founded 1967 and the official Cadillac distributor/dealer in Saudi Arabia and largest GM dealer in the Middle East, is an automotive dealer - an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category regardless of scale.

name: CVD Zahid Tractor
reason: CVD is the Commercial Vehicles Division of Zahid Tractor (Jeddah HQ, est. 1967), the exclusive Saudi distributor of Volvo Trucks, UD Trucks, Renault Trucks, and Volvo/Higer buses. Heavy commercial-vehicle distribution is automotive/industrial, an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category.

name: Decorella Panits EST
reason: Decorella Paints (operated by Zaid Abdul Rahman Al Shalhoub Trading Est, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia) is a paint retail/trading shop. Paint is a construction-material product line closely analogous to the explicitly hard-failed building-materials bucket, and independently a single narrow product line with inherently low repeat-purchase frequency (Gate 2/3 fail). No dedicated live e-commerce website could be found either (only a Facebook page and directory listings), so Gate 4 would independently fail.

name: GRAND HYPER MARKET
reason: Grand Hyper's global HQ is in Dubai, UAE (Regency Group for Corporate Management / 'Grand Corporate', Al Quoz Industrial Area 4), not Qatar. The Qatar outlets (qatar.grandhyper.com, ~8 branches) are a local branch of a UAE-HQ'd retail network spanning UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, KSA and India - this fails Gate 1 geography even though the Qatar operation itself is real, live (online grocery ordering/delivery) and substantial.

name: Jazirat Samaa Fashion
reason: Jazirat Samaa Fashion Co. Ltd (Al Ahsa, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia; ~66-80 employees) is a genuine small Saudi apparel/home-goods retail chain (Gate 1/2/3 pass), but no live, verifiable website or online store could be found for it despite thorough English and Arabic searches. A similarly-described consumer brand ('Samena Stores', samena-stores.com, est. 1992) surfaced in searches but could not be confirmed as the same legal entity, so it was not used to pass this account. No verifiable digital channel found.

name: Juffali Automotive Company
reason: Juffali Automotive Company (JACO), part of the Saudi conglomerate E.A. Juffali & Brothers, is the official Mercedes-Benz general distributor in Saudi Arabia since 1959, with a genuine Saudi HQ (Gate 1 passes). It fails Gate 2: automotive dealer/distributor is an explicit hard-fail category regardless of scale or digital presence.

name: Kia Aljabr I كيا الجبر
reason: Aljabr Trading/Aljabr Holding, headquartered in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, holds the exclusive Kia distributorship for part of the Kingdom since 2008 (Gate 1 passes: genuine Saudi HQ, 28 showrooms, 38 service centers). Fails Gate 2 as an automotive dealer/distributor, a hard-fail category.

name: Kia NMC - الشركة الأهلية للتسويق
reason: National Marketing Company (NMC) is the official Kia distributor for the remaining Saudi regions (Riyadh, Jeddah, Makkah, Madinah, Tabuk, Yanbu, Taif, Abha/Khamis Mushait, Najran, Jizan), operating as a domestic Saudi distributor alongside Aljabr. Automotive dealer/distributor is a hard-fail category (Gate 2) regardless of Saudi operating presence.

name: Kuwait Automotive Imports Company(Al Shaya & Al Sagar)
reason: KAICO, formed by the Kuwaiti Al Shaya and Al Sagar families and operating since 1936 from Al Rai, Kuwait City, is a genuinely Kuwait-HQ'd exclusive distributor for Mazda, Peugeot, Geely and IVECO (Gate 1 passes). Fails Gate 2: automotive dealer/distributor, a hard-fail category.

name: Landmark Arabia
reason: Landmark Arabia is the Saudi operating division of Landmark Group, a conglomerate genuinely headquartered in Dubai, UAE. Per Gate 1, a store run by a UAE-HQ'd group fails geography even with substantial real local operations (650+ stores, 9M+ sq ft, 10,300+ staff including 6,800+ Saudis in KSA since 1994).

name: LubeExSA
reason: LubeExSA is a mobile lubricant/tire-changing service in Saudi Arabia that refers customers to TireEx.com for tire orders; no dedicated official website was found. Regardless of digital presence, automotive parts/tires/lubricant services are an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category (and would also fail Gate 3 as a narrow single-line automotive service).

name: Lubnaas Boutique
reason: Lubnaas is a single-designer ladies'/kids' fashion boutique genuinely based in Doha, Qatar (Gates 1-3 plausible pass: Qatar HQ, fashion, multi-item). However its domain lubnaas.com does not resolve to a working site: the HTTPS endpoint serves a mismatched *.netlify.app wildcard certificate, meaning the custom domain was never properly connected to a live Netlify deployment, so the site is unreachable/broken for real visitors. No cart or checkout was found anywhere; the business appears to operate via phone/in-store only. A follow-up search for an alternate domain found none, only directory listings and a Facebook page, so Gate 4 fails.

name: Mercedes-Benz KSA
reason: This storefront is operated by Juffali Automotive Company, a genuinely Saudi-HQ'd distributor (see Juffali Automotive Company row). Gate 1 passes but Gate 2 hard-fails as an automotive dealer.

name: Mercedes-Benz Kuwait - Al Mulla Automobiles Co.
reason: Al Mulla Automobiles Co., part of the Kuwaiti Al Mulla Group, is a genuinely Kuwait-HQ'd general distributor for Mercedes-Benz since 2019 (Gate 1 passes). Fails Gate 2: automotive dealer, a hard-fail category.

name: Mercedes-Benz Qatar
reason: Operated by Nasser Bin Khaled Automobiles, a genuinely Doha/Qatar-HQ'd distributor established 1957 (Gate 1 passes). Fails Gate 2: automotive dealer, a hard-fail category.

name: Mobil Oil
reason: Mobil-branded lubricants and fuels in Saudi Arabia are distributed by APSCO (Arabian Petroleum Supply Company), a Saudi entity, so a local operating entity does exist there (Gate 1 satisfiable). However the business is wholesale/B2B distribution of petroleum products, lubricants, aviation fuel and marine bunkers, an explicit Gate 2 hard-fail category (non-retail / automotive-fluids-adjacent), not a qualifying consumer retail line.

name: MODERN METAL INDUSTRIES COMPANY
reason: MMICO, headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia since 1997, manufactures cable trays, plastering accessories, steel lintels, expanded metal products, cladding fixation and gypsum profiles for the construction industry (Gate 1 passes: genuine Saudi HQ). Fails Gate 2: building-materials manufacturing/construction B2B is an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Nabina Group مجموعة نابينا
reason: Nabina Group/Nabina Holding, a Doha, Qatar family business since 1951 (Gate 1 would pass), is dominated by building materials (tiles, marble, sanitaryware, kitchens, glass/aluminum, construction tools), architecture/interior design and civil-work contracting, B2B HORECA hotel/restaurant supply, and real-estate consultancy/brokerage -- all explicit Gate 2 hard-fail categories. A small incidental F&B cafe brand ('Loafie') exists but does not change the group's core B2B construction/contracting/real-estate identity, so Gate 2 fails.

name: NBK FASHION
reason: NBK Fashion, the retail-luxury-and-fashion arm of the genuinely Qatar-HQ'd Nasser Bin Khaled conglomerate (Doha, founded 1950), is the official Qatar distributor of Quiksilver, Roxy and DC Shoes (Gates 1-3 plausibly pass: Qatar HQ, fashion, multi-item apparel). However its own domain nbkfashion.net fails to resolve at all (DNS failure), and the brands it distributes are sold online in Qatar only via unrelated third-party marketplaces (Namshi, Noon, Sun & Sand Sports, Next, Vogacloset) that are not NBK Fashion's own channel. No live transactional online store or app of NBK Fashion's own could be confirmed; its presence is limited to physical mall stores (e.g. Doha Festival City) and social media, so Gate 4 fails.

name: Nesto Hypermarket Kuwait
reason: Nesto Hypermarket Kuwait is operated by Nesto Group, part of Western International Group, which is genuinely headquartered in the UAE (Techno Park, Jebel Ali, Dubai), not Kuwait. Per Gate 1, a hypermarket run by a UAE-HQ'd group fails geography even with 20+ real, currently operating outlets in Kuwait.
